name: Queen
hook: The London rock band behind 'Bohemian Rhapsody', whose bass-led 'Another One Bites the Dust' became Weird Al's first parody played live on the radio.
blurb: Queen formed in London in 1970: Freddie Mercury singing and playing piano, Brian May on guitar, Roger Taylor on drums and, from 1971, John Deacon on bass. They recorded mainly for EMI and Elektra. 'Bohemian Rhapsody', from 'A Night at the Opera' (1975), mixed rock, ballad and opera in one six-minute single. 'Another One Bites the Dust', from 'The Game' (1980), built on Deacon's bass line, was a dance hit, and Michael Jackson urged them to release it as a single after seeing them play. Their 1981 'Greatest Hits' became the best-selling album in British history. In 1984 they played nine shows at Sun City in apartheid South Africa, breaking the UN cultural boycott. The band said the audiences were mixed and that they gave money to charity, and the shows were widely criticised. Their 1985 Live Aid set is often called one of the best live performances in rock. Mercury was diagnosed with AIDS in 1987, told the public on 23 November 1991, and died the next day of bronchopneumonia, an illness caused by AIDS. May and Taylor have carried on as Queen, with Adam Lambert singing since 2011.
